note: A PROBE THAT FILTERS ITS DENOMINATOR MUST FILTER ITS NUMERATOR, and the tell is a bucket at EXACTLY 100 percent. The Repose baseline probe tallied land cells under a settleable-land filter but ran its settlement loop unfiltered. Marine settlements sit on ocean cells, so elevation-minus-sea-level went negative and fell through the band classifier into its first band (lowland) as a silent default, while their unrest decile was ranked against a land-only distribution. Detection signature, visible in the committed fixture without rerunning anything: giant-squid 30971 settlements at 100.0 percent lowland, reef-shark 2121 at 100.0 percent, sea-elf 4 at 100.0 percent, zeros in every other band -- while the one land kind in the same table, twig-blight, spread 67/15/13/5 as a real distribution does. Three kinds pinned at exactly 100.0 with exact zeros elsewhere is a default branch, never an ecology. Second tell, cheaper: decile-0 lowland reported 5040 settlements against 4806 land cells. More settlements than cells in the stratum they supposedly occupy. I saw that number, reasoned it away as multi-settlement cells, and missed it -- the ratio of a filtered denominator to an unfiltered numerator is worth one grep every time. Blast radius here: giant-squid alone was 52 percent of the pooled sample, so the pooled row carrying the campaign headline was majority contamination. Nothing went red: a byte-drift check pins bytes and not correctness, and neither preregistered guard bounded it. Related and already in the ledger: settlements in this project can be MARINE, so a sentence of the form this settlement is on land is never safe.
